question: Can a measured, postselected second record change the complete next-first D4 charge law at matched final red-X support on the smallest previously validated chain with genuinely random second outcomes?
role: Bounded exact physical-instrument discriminator, not five-round integration, schedule risk, a general D4 density channel or a threshold
scientific_rationale: The earlier two-edge same-support contrast was exactly null; the six-edge loop has a deterministic second record conditional on first, so it is a weaker measurement-history discriminator. The pinned three-edge chain has complete first/second public laws and nontrivial second randomness under both actions, making it the smallest independent prerequisite before a larger topology or caller integration.
source_basis: Jing Appendix A.2/A.4 ideal red-X and charge projectors
J6L/J6M periodic graph and common vacuum orbit
J6S complete three-edge first/second path law
J7B fixed-path null and frozen caller gap

model.geometry_state: Periodic L=2, pinned 108-qubit J6M common vacuum orbit, private initial red-X chain [0,4,3]; no absolute logical-sector assignment, perfect source projectors and no readout noise
model.shared_first: Measure the complete 24-site binary first public record on the actual initial flux sector; the pinned J6S law has four positive first strings at random sites 1 and 2.
model.branch_a: Public correction [0], then complete action-conditioned second record on residual chain [4,3], then one new private physical red-X fault [4], then measure all eligible next-first stars on final support [3]. Pinned J6S has eight positive first/second prefixes; the second site-0 bit is genuinely random.
model.branch_b: Public correction [0,4], then complete action-conditioned second record on residual edge [3], then zero future physical fault and a fresh complete next-first readout on the same final support [3]. Pinned J6S has sixteen positive first/second prefixes; the second sites 0 and 1 vary. No-fault projector idempotence must be checked explicitly on the random sites.
model.private_public_boundary: Physical supports, future-fault edge, ordered projector masks, prepared orbit and postselected state remain private. Only action IDs, full 24-site binary flux/charge/vacuum arrays and causal digests may enter a public completion. Defer and the frozen five-round caller are not invoked in this matrix.
model.matched_exogenous_keys: One private physical key and four enumerated first keys are shared across both actions. Each branch enumerates its complete second exogenous outcomes; branch A uses one fixed future-fault key. No stochastic seed, history resampling or bootstrap is used.
model.independent_unit_and_uncertainty: One exact prepared orbit and geometry; rational Born probabilities and exact total variation, not stochastic estimates or intervals. A null or positive finite contrast is not a general D4 theorem.

matrix.exact_law: For each branch A positive pinned J6S first/second prefix, use chronological first/second/next-first projector moments on the actual postselected state, classify every eligible next-site conditional, and enumerate the full joint law over all variable sites into 24-site public arrays. For branch B, verify sitewise no-new-fault exact repeat at both random second sites and use complete J6S second records as the next-first law by commuting-projector idempotence.
matrix.discriminator: At each of four identical first public strings, marginalize the branch-specific second record, compare the two complete next-first public laws at matched final red-X support [3], and record exact rational total variation. Nonzero supports finite history sensitivity; zero is a bounded negative result. Do not call it an isolated correction effect because second measurement sectors and physical-fault timing differ.
matrix.structural_caller_gate: Require the frozen five-round caller hash to remain pinned and retain the earlier J7B not-integrated status; do not implement or execute caller evaluation unless a separately validated physical law and adapter contract are registered.

competing_outcomes.history_sensitive: At least one first record has a nonzero exact full-public total variation despite identical final red-X support.
competing_outcomes.support_only_on_fixture: All four exact contrasts have total variation zero; this narrows but does not establish general sufficiency of current support.
competing_outcomes.censored: If a full next-first law exceeds the registered variable-site, moment, row or CPU cap, retain the censor and valid one-site diagnostics only; make no full-public contrast claim.

acceptance: All six pins pass before and after; J6S branch rows and first/second masses reproduce exactly

Both independent branches honor complete 24-site binary public records and actual-sector eligibility/commutation; branch A full next-first law normalizes and branch B no-fault repeat is independently checked or explicitly censored
The four matched-first full-public total variations are exact only when both branches close; all prefix/action/public-private integrity and replay checks pass
No frozen-caller mutation or invocation, no new dependency, and zero stochastic histories, schedule arms and bootstrap replicates
The conclusion remains one ideal fixed chain; no general physical feedback kernel, noisy JIT advantage, scaling or threshold claim
stop_rule: Pin and validate both J6S branches before exact computation. Execute branch A and branch B at their fixed geometry/actions/future faults; censor a branch at its original cap and do not enlarge, change the future edge or infer a full-public contrast from selected sites. Fail closed on source, sector, commutation, normalization, first/second provenance, public/private, action binding or replay drift. Caller integration remains dependent and unexecuted in this tick.
